newsitem.title: GERMANY: Market nerves seen further weighing on German DAX.
newsitem.headline: Market nerves seen further weighing on German DAX.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse was expected to continue to suffer from a bout of nerves after both stocks and bonds dropped on Wednesday as worries about excessive market strength re-emerged.

The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day trade in the DAX index of 30 top German shares, came off a day's low of 2,819.68 points to trade down 51.81 points at 2,839.14 points by 1525 GMT, encouraged as Wall Street pared early losses and the dollar recovered above 1.54 marks.
But dealers said there was still some residual nervousness in the market and the dollar and Dow would be closely watched.
Dealers said a fall on Friday, promted by comments by Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan about "irrational exuberance" in global asset markets, was still causing nerves.
"Greenspan is still making people edgy. We are extra-sensitive to any move down," said one trader.

By Tuesday the DAX had almost recouped all the losses posted on Friday rising up near the 2,900 point level and dealers said that markets had possibly recovered too quickly after the Greenspan warning.
"Greenspan did not say something like that for fun and he is a man who wants to be taken seriously," said one trader.

Dealers said that a Wall Street Journal article suggesting that a slowdown in Japanese purchases of U.S. debt could depress U.S. markets, had also prompted fears. But U.S. Treasuries managed to pick themselves up and pare some losses on Wednesday, also encouraging German Bunds.

On Thursday, attention will turn to U.S consumer price data, due out at 1330 GMT, expected to rise 0.3 percent in November. November producer prices released on Wednesday rose 0.4 percent, more than expected, but were balanced out by a less-than-expected rise in core prices of 0.1 percent.
